question: What is the main goal of pain management after an abortion?

options.A: To keep the patient asleep all day
options.B: To stop the patient from asking for drugs
options.C: To stop all physical feelings in the pelvis
options.D: To reduce recovery time and prevent severe discomfort

explanation: Managing post-abortion pain effectively helps patients recover faster and stops acute pain from turning into long-term problems. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h1)

question: Why do some patients avoid reporting pain after an abortion?

options.A: An allergy to standard pain medications
options.B: Fear of being judged or feeling they must endure it quietly
options.C: A lack of nerve endings in the uterus
options.D: The use of local nerve blocks

explanation: Patients often hide their discomfort due to personal beliefs or worries about how healthcare workers will react. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h1)

question: What causes cramping pain after the uterus is emptied?

options.A: Gas trapped in the large intestine
options.C: Rhythmic uterine contractions driven by prostaglandins
options.D: A sudden drop in blood pressure

explanation: The uterus squeezes tightly using prostaglandins to stop bleeding, which creates strong cramps. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h2)

question: Sharp lower belly discomfort during the procedure is mostly linked to what?

options.A: Filling of the bladder with urine
options.B: Inflammation of the skin fat layer
options.D: Relaxation of pelvic muscles from anesthesia

explanation: Opening the tight cervix with instruments stimulates pain receptors, causing distinct pressure and sharp discomfort. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h2)

question: How often should pain levels be checked right after the procedure?

options.A: Only during the doctor's morning rounds
options.B: Only when the patient cries out
options.C: Whenever routine vital signs are checked

explanation: Checking pain levels at the same time as blood pressure and pulse ensures quick identification of distress. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: Which pain scale is best for a patient who cannot speak English or read numbers?
explanation: The faces scale allows patients to point to a drawing that shows how they feel without needing words. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: How does ibuprofen help in post-abortion care?

options.A: By increasing blood pressure to the pelvic organs
options.B: By lowering prostaglandin production to ease cramping
options.C: By blocking all nerve signals in the brain
options.D: By relaxing the muscles of the abdominal wall

explanation: Ibuprofen stops the body from making the chemicals that cause the uterus to cramp hard. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: A patient has severe pelvic pain that does not improve with oral ibuprofen. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Stop giving all future pain medications
options.B: Note that the patient has a low pain tolerance
options.C: Notify the prescriber to check for stronger medications or issues
options.D: Tell the patient to walk around the ward

explanation: Unrelieved pain can signal a developing complication like retained tissue, requiring medical review. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: How does a warm compress on the lower belly help reduce pain?

options.A: It numbs the skin nerves with cold
options.B: It stimulates the kidneys to make urine
options.C: It increases bleeding by opening surface vessels
options.D: It relaxes uterine muscles to ease cramping

explanation: Heat helps the uterine muscle fibers relax, which decreases the intensity of menstrual-like cramps. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h5)

question: Which body position helps relieve tension on the pelvic muscles during recovery?

options.A: Flat on the back with legs straight
options.C: Sitting upright on a hard chair
options.D: Lying on the side with knees bent

explanation: Curling slightly to the side with bent knees takes the strain off the lower abdomen and pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h5)

question: Which symptom shows normal recovery after an abortion?

options.A: A sudden high fever forty-eight hours later
options.B: Lower abdominal pain that gets worse every day
options.C: Severe pain felt only in the right shoulder
options.D: Cramping pain that slowly gets better over days

explanation: Standard recovery involves mild to moderate cramps that fade away as the uterus heals. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)

question: Why are pain, bad-smelling discharge, and fever a major concern?

options.A: They strongly suggest a pelvic infection
options.B: They mean the pain relievers are too weak
options.C: They prove the patient is allergic to antibiotics
options.D: They are a normal reaction to cervical stretching

explanation: Fever and bad-smelling discharge point to bacterial growth inside the uterus that needs urgent treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)

question: What advice should a nurse give about taking pain medication at home?

options.A: Take medications on a regular schedule before pain gets bad
options.B: Double the dose if cramping feels uncomfortable
options.C: Stop taking all pain pills right after leaving the clinic
options.D: Wait until pain is severe before taking pills

explanation: Taking analgesics on time keeps blood levels steady and stops pain from getting out of control. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h7)

question: Why does the nurse advise patients to avoid vaginal douches during discharge counseling?

options.B: To keep the outer genital area completely dry
options.C: To prevent washing away oral pills
options.D: To prevent introducing bacteria and causing a pelvic infection

explanation: Putting liquids or objects into the vagina too early can push germs upward into the healing uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h7)
